ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: Gimme Some Slack
ModMetaData.author: Mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
Power cables with some slack in them. Gimme Some Slack swaps the straight grey conduit for loose, too-long cords lying on the floor, and adds real overhead power lines strung between masts.
Floor cords: conduit still works exactly like vanilla conduit; only the drawing changes. The mod reads each power net as a graph of the things it connects (generators, batteries, machines, junctions, and the places where a run dives into a wall or rock and comes out again) and draws loose cords between connected neighbours over the walkable floor. Cords never cross a wall and never join two things that are not really connected; where a cord has to pass under a wall, a plate marks the crossing. Breaks read at a glance: a conduit end still on a powered net sparks, a dead end lies limp. Selecting a powered building highlights every cord on its net. Nothing about the cords is saved, so adding or removing them mid-game is safe; the power overlay's connection lines are left alone.
Overhead lines: power masts, lamp masts and wall brackets carry real power over open ground on sagging wires that sway in the wind and may pass over roofed rooms. Explosions can cut a wire: the cut ends hang from their insulators and spark while live, shock whoever touches them and can light spilled fuel, and colonists can re-string them. A power-tap clamp quietly drains another faction's grid into yours without merging the two, and getting caught can cost goodwill. Unlike the cords these are real buildings with saved links: removing the mod from a save that holds them loses them, with missing-definition errors.
Four looks: Scrapper, Industrial, Modern and Futuristic, picked per build on the build button (Mod Settings sets the default). Everything lives in one Mod Settings entry with two tabs, Cables and Overhead lines; every behaviour has its own switch, and each master switch brings the vanilla art straight back.
The flexible hoses that used to live here now ship in RimMandrake: FlowWorks.
Requires Harmony and all five RimWorld expansions.
